title: Finite degree and global sections under compatible field and scheme isomorphisms
statement: Let $K,L$ be fields, let $\varphi:K\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ be a field isomorphism and put $j=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi):\operatorname{Spec}L\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $Z,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $h:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, $q:T\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ structure morphisms, and $u:T\xrightarrow{\sim}Z$ an isomorphism satisfying $h\circ u=j\circ q$. Give $A=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ and $B=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ the algebra structures $\alpha:K\to A$ and $\beta:L\to B$ induced by $h$ and $q$. Then $u^*:A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ is a ring isomorphism satisfying $u^*\circ\alpha=\beta\circ\varphi$, hence $u^*(\alpha(a)v)=\beta(\varphi(a))u^*(v)$ for all $a\in K$ and $v\in A$. For any index set $I$, a family $(v_i)_{i\in I}$ is a $K$-basis of $A$ if and only if $(u^*v_i)_{i\in I}$ is an $L$-basis of $B$. Moreover, $h$ is finite if and only if $q$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. When they are finite, their degrees [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound] satisfy $\dim_K A=\dim_L B$, with the dimensions taken using precisely $\alpha$ and $\beta$.

proof.text: Apply global sections to $h\circ u=j\circ q$. By the composition formula this says $e\circ h^*=q^*\circ j^*$. The statement [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-global-sections] with $\psi=\varphi$ identifies $j^*$ with $\varphi$ through the canonical identifications $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}K,\mathcal O)=K$ and $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}L,\mathcal O)=L$. Consequently $e\circ\alpha=\beta\circ\varphi$. Multiplicativity of $e$ now gives $e(\alpha(a)v)=e(\alpha(a))e(v)=\beta(\varphi(a))e(v)$. Inverting this identity gives $e^{-1}(\beta(b)w)=\alpha(\varphi^{-1}(b))e^{-1}(w)$.

proof.text: Use the private proved helper transport_basis: for a semilinear equivalence f:M ≃ₛₗ[φ] N and an R-basis b indexed by I, form the S-linear equivalence N → (I →₀ S) by composing f⁻¹, b.repr, and Finsupp.mapRange.linearEquiv φ.toSemilinearEquiv. The scalar homomorphisms compose to the identity, so Basis.ofRepr gives an S-basis. Its vector at i is f(b i), since the coefficient equivalence fixes the single coefficient 1. For global sections take f to have additive equivalence e.toAddEquiv and prove its semilinearity by step 2 using precisely h.ΓAlgebra and q.ΓAlgebra. Apply the helper to f and to f.symm, respectively, and use e.symm_apply_apply to obtain both directions of the basis assertion. No finiteness or nonemptiness of I is needed.

proof.text: The field equivalence φ is bijective, so CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom is an isomorphism and so is its image under Spec. Mathlib gives IsFinite a RespectsIso instance from its multiplicativity [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] and finiteness of isomorphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply MorphismProperty.cancel_left_of_respectsIso to u.hom and h, rewrite by comm, and apply cancel_right_of_respectsIso to q and Spec.map φ. This yields IsFinite h iff IsFinite q.

proof.text: Install exactly the algebra structures h.ΓAlgebra and q.ΓAlgebra. Apply Mathlib Algebra.finrank_eq_of_equiv_equiv to φ and e with the symmetric ring-map compatibility of step 2. The result is the equality of finrankΓ by its definition [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound], using Module.finrank [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. This argument applies even without finite-dimensionality, and hence proves the stated implication from IsFinite h, including the zero-ring case.
